title: Operating Point and DC Sweeps
intro: The operating point is the DC solution with capacitors open and inductors shorted. Every other analysis starts from it, and most simulation trouble shows up first here. A DC sweep repeats it while one or two sources, a resistor or the temperature change.

blocks.source:
Operating point of a resistively loaded common-source stage
.model nch NMOS (level=1 vto=0.5 kp=200u lambda=0.05)
VDD vdd 0 1.8
VG  g   0 0.8
RD  vdd d 10k
M1  d g 0 0 nch W=4u L=1u
.control
  op
  print v(d) i(VDD)
  show M1 : id gm gds vdsat
  print @m1[id] @m1[gm]
  let av = -@m1[gm] * 10k / (1 + @m1[gds]*10k)
  print av
.endc
.end

blocks.text: The op result is a plot with one value per vector: node voltages v(n) and branch currents of voltage sources and inductors, i(V1) (also written v1#branch). show prints the operating-point quantities of a device; @dev[par] reads one into an expression. Above, the stage gain follows from gm and gds: -gm RD / (1 + gds RD). In batch mode, .op prints a table of all node voltages and source currents unless .option noinit is set; .option opinfo (or the command option opinfo) adds device data.
How ngspice finds the operating point

items: First a plain Newton-Raphson iteration from zero (or from .nodeset values), up to itl1 iterations (default 100).
If that fails, gmin stepping (gminsteps option, default on): start with a large conductance across every junction and reduce it step by step, each solution starting the next.
Then source stepping (srcsteps, default on): ramp all sources from zero to their full value.
Optionally a transient operating point (optran): a short transient with the sources ramped up, whose end point becomes the operating point. Recommended for big digital-heavy or oscillating circuits.
The Convergence page explains what to do when all of these fail.

.nodeset v(n1)=0.9 v(n2)=0: starting guesses for the iteration. The final answer is free to move away from them. Use them to pick one state of a bistable circuit (a latch, a Schmitt trigger) or to help a hard circuit converge.
.ic v(n1)=0.9: forces the node to that voltage during the initial operating point of a transient, then lets it go. It affects only transient analysis (Transient page).
off on a device line: start the iteration with that device off.

blocks.source:
* .dc srcname start stop step [src2 start2 stop2 step2]
.dc VIN 0 1.8 0.01                 $ a voltage or current source
.dc VDS 0 1.8 0.05 VGS 0.4 1.2 0.2 $ nested: VDS inner, VGS outer
.dc RLOAD 1k 10k 1k                $ a resistor's value
.dc TEMP -40 125 5                 $ the circuit temperature

blocks.text: DC sweeps of a parameter are not built in, but a control-language loop with alterparam and reset does it (Sweeps page), and a source whose value is a parameter can stand in. In a nested sweep the results go into one long vector per output; to plot one curve per outer value, loop in the control language.

blocks.source:
Inverter transfer curve and its gain, then a temperature sweep
.model nch NMOS (level=1 vto=0.5 kp=200u lambda=0.05)
.model pch PMOS (level=1 vto=-0.5 kp=80u lambda=0.05)
VDD vdd 0 1.8
VIN in  0 0
MP out in vdd vdd pch W=5u L=1u
MN out in 0   0   nch W=2u L=1u
.control
  dc VIN 0 1.8 0.005
  let gain = deriv(v(out))
  meas dc vm   when v(out)=v(in)
  meas dc gmax min gain
  meas dc vil  when gain=-1 cross=1
  meas dc vih  when gain=-1 cross=2
  alter VIN 0.9
  dc TEMP -40 125 55
  print v(out)
.endc
.end

blocks.text: deriv() differentiates a vector against its scale (here v(in)), giving the small-signal gain at every point; the points where the gain is -1 are the input thresholds VIL and VIH used for noise margins. With equal kp W/L of both devices (200u x 2 = 80u x 5) the switching point is at VDD/2.

By default only voltage-source and inductor currents are saved. To get the current of a resistor, capacitor or transistor terminal, either put a 0 V source in series, read @R1[i] or @M1[id] (save them first in a sweep: save all @m1[id]), or set .option savecurrents, which saves the terminal currents of every device as vectors named @m1[id], @r1[i] and so on (this makes rawfiles much larger).

blocks.title: Bistable start
blocks.text: A cross-coupled latch always settles to the same state at the operating point, but you need the other one. Two ways?
solution: .nodeset v(q)=1.8 v(qb)=0 (the iteration starts there and stays in that basin).
Or put off on the transistor that should be off; or in a transient, .ic v(q)=1.8 v(qb)=0.

blocks.title: Gain from the op
blocks.text: In the sample, the op gives @m1[gm] = 0.257 mS and @m1[gds] = 1.8 uS. Check the printed gain, and the drain current from the level 1 equations.
solution: Level 1 saturation: Id = (kp/2)(W/L)(Vgs - Vt)^2 (1 + lambda Vds) = 100u x 4 x 0.09 x (1 + 0.05 x 1.41) = 36 uA x 1.07 = 38.5 uA, matching i(VDD).

items: H. Vogt, G. Atkinson, D. Warning and P. Nenzi, Ngspice User's Manual, version 47, 2026 (ngspice.sourceforge.io/docs.html), sections 11.2 (initial conditions), 11.3.2 (.dc) and 11.3.5 (.op).
